outcome: Since 26 January 2024 nothing in scope has settled Graham's conjecture, bounded its own quantity for all graphs, or proved a new family of cases that I could verify. The only in-window item that bears directly on the conjecture is Pulaj, Wood and Yerger (arXiv 2411.19314, 28 Nov 2024), which checks a support-restricted pebbling number for all 22 pairs of 8-vertex Lemke graphs and is explicitly not a proof; a 2025 PJM abstract framed by the conjecture (2t-pebbling of bipartite graphs) could not be read in full. Wikipedia's article, last edited 25 Dec 2025, still lists the conjecture as unsolved, and a March 2026 seminar titled after it claims no new result.
problem_asks: Whether, for all connected graphs G and H (the statement says graphs; every source restricts to connected graphs), the pebbling number of the Cartesian product G□H is at most the product π(G)·π(H), where π is the standard pebbling number: the least n such that from any distribution of n pebbles on the graph one can move a pebble to any chosen vertex. Parts: (1) the universal claim over all pairs (G, H); (2) the single inequality π(G□H) ≤ π(G)π(H) as the whole claim; (3) the standard pebbling number on each factor and on the product (not optimal pebbling, threshold pebbling, rubbling, t-pebbling or cover pebbling). The statement names one conjecture and asks nothing else. A case settles part of it only if it covers a class of pairs (G, H); a single pair or a restricted configuration class is an instance, not the universal claim.

events.what_happened: Herscovici, Hester and Hurlbert, 'Generalizations of Graham's Pebbling Conjecture' (arXiv 0905.3197, posted 19 May 2009). The abstract says they develop machinery for the conjecture, 'now twenty years old', show that certain conjectures imply others that initially appear stronger, give counterexamples to Sjöstrand's cover-pebbling theorem when edge-dependent transfer costs are allowed, and 'describe an alternate pebbling number for which Graham's conjecture is demonstrably false'. The abstract does not say the standard pebbling number is false. Discounted for this bullet: the falsity is for a different quantity.
events.delivers: For the alternate pebbling number (defined in the full text, which I did not read), the product inequality fails. It establishes nothing about the standard π(G□H) ≤ π(G)π(H).
events.remains: The standard-pebbling inequality for all connected G and H, which is the whole of problem_asks.
events.directly_checkable: Not from the abstract. The alternate definition and the counterexample are in the full paper, which I did not open.
events.doubts: The alternate number is not defined in the text I could read, so I cannot judge how far it departs from π. Hurlbert and Seddiq (arXiv 2011.10623, 2020) cite the 2009 paper for the Target Conjecture, not for this falsity. I found no public check of the falsity claim.
events.direction: Cuts against the product inequality, but only for a variant pebbling number, not for the quantity the problem names.
events.object: Not described in the abstract: an alternate pebbling number under which the product inequality fails. The explicit counterexample is in the full text, which I did not open.

events.what_happened: Herscovici, Hester and Hurlbert, 'Optimal Pebbling in Products of Graphs' (arXiv 0907.5577, posted 31 July 2009). The abstract says they 'prove a generalization of Graham's Conjecture for optimal pebbling with arbitrary sets of target distributions', give bounds for optimal pebbling of products of complete graphs, find explicit optimal t-pebbling numbers for some such products, bound optimal pebbling of powers of C5, and give asymptotic bounds for hypercubes. Discounted: optimal pebbling is a different quantity from the standard π.
events.revisions: v1 only (31 July 2009). A journal version appears as Australas. J. Combin. 50 (listing at ajc-new.maths.uq.edu.au/v50.p003, not opened).
events.delivers: A generalization of the product inequality for optimal pebbling with arbitrary target sets, and bounds on products of complete graphs, powers of C5 and hypercubes, all for the optimal pebbling number. Nothing for the standard π.
events.remains: The standard-pebbling inequality for all connected G and H.

checked_by.who: Australasian Journal of Combinatorics (journal version, volume 50)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the version (I did not open it; venue from a search excerpt only)

events.doubts: None specific to the claim. The result is for a different pebbling number, so it is not evidence about the standard conjecture either way.
events.direction: Positive for a variant quantity (optimal pebbling); neutral for the standard one.

events.what_happened: Hurlbert, 'A linear optimization technique for graph pebbling' (arXiv 1101.5641, posted 28 Jan 2011). Introduces the Weight Function Lemma, an LP tool for upper bounds on pebbling numbers, applied to the Petersen graph, the Lemke graph, the Lemke square ('Lemke squared'), the 4th weak Bruhat graph, trees, cycles and cubes. The abstract gives no numerical bound for the Lemke square. Kenter et al. (2019) and Flocco et al. (2023) both attribute a bound of 108 on π(L□L) to this line of work; I could not confirm the 108 value from the abstract, and the body was not read.
events.delivers: A method. For the Lemke square it gives the attributed bound 108 on π(L□L), which is a bound on one instance of the product inequality and not a decision on it.
events.remains: The conjecture for all G and H, and π(L□L) ≤ 64 for the Lemke square.
events.doubts: The 108 figure is attributed to this paper by two later papers but is not visible in the abstract I read. The later work uses the method rather than verifying this paper's claims.
events.direction: Neutral: an upper bound on a Lemke-square instance above the conjectured 64.

events.what_happened: Xia, Pan and Xu, 'Pebbling on C_{4k+3}×G and M(C_{2n})×G' (arXiv 1402.0764, v1 4 Feb 2014, v2 6 Feb 2014). The abstract says that if G has the odd two-pebbling property, then f(C_{4k+3}×G) ≤ f(C_{4k+3})f(G) and f(M(C_{2n})×G) ≤ f(M(C_{2n}))f(G), where M(C_{2n}) is the middle graph of an even cycle. No journal reference on the arXiv page.
events.delivers: The product inequality when one factor is an odd cycle C_{4k+3} or the middle graph of an even cycle, and the other factor has the odd two-pebbling property (a hypothesis the abstract does not define).
events.remains: All other pairs (G, H), including any pair where neither factor is of those types or the second factor lacks the odd two-pebbling property. The general inequality.
events.doubts: The argument depends on the odd two-pebbling property, which the arXiv page does not define; I did not read the body.
events.direction: Positive for the factor pairs named; consistent with the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Cranston, Postle, Xue and Yerger, 'Modified Linear Programming and Class 0 Bounds for Graph Pebbling' (arXiv 1508.07299, posted 28 Aug 2015; J. Combin. Optim. 34(1), 2017, pp. 114–132 per the arXiv journal-reference field). Improves Hurlbert's LP technique with weight functions on graphs more general than trees, giving improved pebbling bounds for some of Hurlbert's graphs, and proves an edge bound for Class 0 graphs that disproves a conjecture of Blasiak et al. The abstract does not mention Lemke graphs or Cartesian products.
events.delivers: Improved pebbling-number bounds for some graphs and a Class 0 edge bound. Neither is a product bound.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. I did not check whether any of the improved bounds apply to a Lemke product; the abstract is silent.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published (34(1), 2017), per the arXiv journal-reference field

events.direction: Neutral for the product inequality; a tool paper for pebbling bounds.

events.what_happened: Watson and Green (students), with mentors Charles Cusack and Airat Bekmetjev, 'Graham's Conjecture, Lemke Graphs, and Algorithms', poster at Hope College's 15th Annual Celebration of Undergraduate Research and Creative Performance (event date 15 April 2016). The abstract says the authors 'will show that Graham's conjecture holds for such families as Lk□Kn and several others', and that Lemke graphs are the only known graphs lacking the two-pebbling property. The full paper is marked unavailable on the repository page.
events.delivers: A stated intention to prove the conjecture for Lk□Kn and other families. No proof is visible in what I could read, so nothing is established on this record.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.doubts: A poster abstract stating a goal, not a result; the proof is not visible. A search excerpt (2024-era) says Gao and Yin proved the conjecture for L□K_n, but I could not retrieve that paper, so the attribution is unverified.
events.direction: Stated as a positive intention; no result in the record.

events.what_happened: Xia, Pan, Xu and Cheng, 'Graham's pebbling conjecture on Cartesian product of the middle graphs of even cycles' (arXiv 1705.00191, posted 29 Apr 2017). The abstract says the paper gives pebbling numbers of some graphs and proves that Graham's conjecture holds for the middle graphs of some even cycles. DBLP lists it as Ars Combinatoria 132 (2017) 285–294 under a slightly different title (from a search excerpt, not opened). A search summary said Journal of Combinatorial Optimization; I found no support for that.
events.delivers: The product inequality for the Cartesian product of the middle graph of some even cycles with a second factor whose condition the abstract does not state.
events.remains: All other factor pairs and the general inequality.
events.doubts: The abstract does not state the hypothesis on the second factor. The 2014 companion paper by overlapping authors needed the odd two-pebbling property, so the same hypothesis is likely but I did not read the body to confirm it.
events.direction: Positive for the factor pairs named; consistent with the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Asplund, Hurlbert and Kenter, 'Pebbling on graph products and other binary graph constructions' (arXiv 1801.07808, posted 23 Jan 2018; Australas. J. Combin. 71(2) 2018, pp. 246–260 per a search excerpt). Proves π(G□H) ≤ 2π(G)π(H) and the sharper π(G□H) ≤ (π(G)+|G|)π(H) for all graphs. The abstract states the conjecture as Graham's and proves only these weaker bounds.
events.revisions: v1 only (arXiv). Journal version per search excerpt.
events.delivers: General product upper bounds with constant 2 and an additive |G| term, valid for all G and H. These are weaker than the conjectured bound and do not settle any instance of it.
events.remains: The inequality π(G□H) ≤ π(G)π(H) itself, for all G and H.
events.direction: Partial: a weaker general bound. It does not go the way of the conjecture or against it.

events.what_happened: Pleanmani, 'Graham's pebbling conjecture holds for the product of a graph and a sufficiently large complete bipartite graph', Discrete Mathematics, Algorithms and Applications 6(11), 2019, DOI 10.1142/S179383091950068X (OpenAlex publication date 27 Sep 2019). Cited on Wikipedia's Graph pebbling page as a partial result. I did not read the paper; title, venue and year come from a Khon Kaen University faculty listing and the OpenAlex record.
events.delivers: The product inequality when H is a complete bipartite graph of sufficiently large order (the threshold is not read).
events.remains: H complete bipartite below the threshold, all other H, and all pairs of graphs.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published; its refereeing was not checked

events.doubts: Only the title and listing were read. The 'sufficiently large' threshold is unknown to me.
events.direction: Positive for the complete-bipartite-H case named in the title.

events.what_happened: Kenter, Skipper and Wilson, 'Computing Bounds on Product-Graph Pebbling Numbers' (arXiv 1905.08683, v1 21 May 2019, the only version listed; 27 pp). An integer-programming (partial-pebbling) model gives π(L□L) ≤ 85 for the Lemke graph L (8 vertices, π(L)=8), improving on 91 (Kenter and Skipper, earlier model) and on 108 (attributed to Hurlbert). The paper also reports the exact pebbling numbers, found by the model, for products of Lemke-type graphs with K8, K12, K4,4 and K6,6. The conjectured value for L□L is 64, so 85 neither confirms nor refutes it. An earlier version appeared as 'Integer-Programming Bounds on Pebbling Numbers of Cartesian-Product Graphs' (Springer, 2018; from a search excerpt, not opened). Note: a search summary attributed this result to 'Cusack and Bekmetjev'; the arXiv authors are Kenter, Skipper and Wilson.
events.delivers: An upper bound π(L□L) ≤ 85 on one instance (the Lemke square), and exact values for finitely many specific products of Lemke-type graphs with complete and complete bipartite graphs. None of these is a case of the universal claim.
events.remains: π(L□L) between 64 and 85 is unresolved. Everything else in problem_asks.
events.directly_checkable: Not by hand. The bound rests on an integer program with no exact certificate given in the text I read.
events.doubts: The computation uses Gurobi 8.1.0 with floating-point arithmetic, and the paper says the bounds were not verified by an exact rational solver (read from the ar5iv body). The 2023 Flocco et al. introduction, in the part I read, says it improves 108 to 96 and does not mention 85, so the two lines of work are not reconciled in the text I read.
events.direction: Neutral: an upper bound of 85 is consistent with the conjectured 64 and does not establish it. It is a bound on one instance.

ai.disclosed_cost: Gurobi 8.1.0 with Python and Pyomo (per the body; version numbers for those two not checked). Computing time not read. This is a MIP solver, not AI.

events.what_happened: Cusack, Green, Bekmetjev and Powers, 'Graph pebbling algorithms and Lemke graphs', Discrete Applied Mathematics 262 (2019) 72–82, DOI 10.1016/j.dam.2019.02.028. Gives algorithms for reachability and solvability of configurations and classifies all Lemke graphs (graphs lacking the two-pebbling property) on at most nine vertices, finding many previously unknown ones. The PDF could not be read through the fetch tool (binary response), so this description comes from search excerpts. A seminar titled 'Graph Pebbling Algorithms and Graham's Conjecture' (Aaron Green, RPI, 17 March 2026, opened) repeats the nine-vertex classification and makes no claim about the conjecture; it is not counted as a new event.
events.delivers: A classification of Lemke graphs up to nine vertices and reachability and solvability algorithms. The excerpts show no product bound.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.doubts: Described from search excerpts only. Lemke graphs are the natural factors for a counterexample, so the classification bears on the question but does not move it.
events.direction: Neutral: supplies the candidate factors (Lemke graphs). No product result in the excerpts.

events.what_happened: Pleanmani, 'Graham's Pebbling Conjecture Holds for the Product of a Graph and a Sufficiently Large Complete Graph', Theory and Applications of Graphs 7(1), article 1, 2020, DOI 10.20429/tag.2020.070101. The abstract says that for connected G and H, the inequality π(G□H) ≤ π(G)π(H) holds when H is a complete graph of sufficiently large order in terms of graph parameters of G. The repository page shows 'Since January 06, 2020'.
events.delivers: The product inequality when H is a complete graph K_m with m large relative to parameters of G. No explicit threshold is given in the abstract.
events.remains: H a complete graph below the threshold, H not complete, and all pairs of graphs.
events.doubts: The threshold 'sufficiently large' is not explicit, and I did not read the body.

events.what_happened: Li and Ye, 'The 2-pebbling property of squares of paths and Graham's conjecture', Open Mathematics 18(1) (2020) 87–92, DOI 10.1515/math-2020-0009, published 10 March 2020 (from a search excerpt). The De Gruyter and DOAJ pages returned errors, so I read only the search excerpt.

events.remains: Other graph pairs, and any part of the square-of-path cases not covered. Unverified.

events.what_happened: Hurlbert and Seddiq, 'On the Target Pebbling Conjecture' (arXiv 2011.10623; v1 20 Nov 2020, v2 10 May 2021, v3 20 Dec 2021). Proves the Target Conjecture of Herscovici, Hester and Hurlbert (2009) for 2-paths and for Kneser graphs over pairs. The abstract calls Graham's 1989 product conjecture 'famous' and says the Target Conjecture could help attack it. It does not claim to resolve the product conjecture, and its treatment implies the conjecture is open.
events.revisions: v2 10 May 2021; v3 20 Dec 2021 (retitled from 'The Target Pebbling Conjecture').
events.delivers: The Target Conjecture for 2-paths and Kneser graphs over pairs. This is not a case of the product inequality.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.

events.what_happened: Pleanmani, Nupo and Worawiset, 'Bounds for the pebbling number of product graphs', Transactions on Combinatorics 11(4) (2022) 317–326, DOI 10.22108/toc.2021.128705.1855. Received 15 May 2021, accepted 1 Oct 2021, published online 1 Dec 2022. Lowers the general bound from 2π(G)π(H) to (2 − 1/min{π(G),π(H)})π(G)π(H) for the Cartesian product, and discusses strong products, cross products and coronas. The abstract does not state the conjecture as proved.
events.delivers: A general upper bound for all G and H with factor (2 − 1/min) below 2 but still above 1. It is weaker than the conjectured bound and settles no instance of it.
events.remains: The inequality π(G□H) ≤ π(G)π(H) for all G and H.

events.what_happened: Yang, Yerger and Zhou, 'Lollipop and Cubic Weight Functions for Graph Pebbling' (arXiv 2310.00580; v1 1 Oct 2023, v2 24 Nov 2024). Constructs a non-tree weight function for Q4, a set of valid weight functions for lollipop variants, and states a conjecture on weight functions for the n-cube. The abstract does not mention Graham's conjecture or L□L. A search excerpt says the body asks whether these weight functions can improve π(L□L); I did not confirm this. Journal version: J. Combin. Optim. 49(1), 2025 (DOI 10.1007/s10878-024-01248-1, from an IDEAS listing; not opened).

events.what_happened: Flocco, Pulaj and Yerger, 'Automating Weight Function Generation in Graph Pebbling' (arXiv 2312.12618, v1 only, 19 Dec 2023). A MILP framework generates tree-strategy weight functions with certificates. It gives π(B4) ≤ 66 for the 4th weak Bruhat graph and π(L×L) ≤ 96 for the Lemke square. The abstract does not mention Graham's conjecture; the body (read to character 100,000 of about 105,000) states it as Conjecture 2.1 and says L may be a counterexample. The introduction says the result improves the bound of 108 from Hurlbert. For some roots the paper reports bounds close to 64, occasionally equal to it.
events.delivers: Certificates giving π(L□L) ≤ 96 and per-root bounds close to 64 for some roots, all from tree-strategy weight functions. Not a proof that π(L□L) ≤ 64. Also π(B4) ≤ 66, which is unrelated to the product.
events.remains: Whether π(L□L) ≤ 64, and every other pair of graphs.
events.directly_checkable: The certificates are weight functions that can be checked by hand, according to the paper. The text does not state an exact-arithmetic verification of them, and the computations were run in Gurobi and CPLEX.
events.doubts: The paper says the certificates avoid floating-point error and can be checked by hand, but it also says the computation used Gurobi and CPLEX. I did not find an independent exact check. The 'best attainable with tree strategies' claim is a belief, not a proof of optimality.
events.direction: Neutral: upper bounds 96 on L□L (above 64) and near-64 bounds for some roots. It does not reach the threshold that would disprove the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Charton, Ellenberg, Wagner and Williamson, 'PatternBoost: Constructions in Mathematics with a Little Help from AI' (arXiv 2411.00566, v1 1 Nov 2024). The abstract reports a counterexample to a conjecture open for 30 years. A CERMICS news page (search excerpt, not opened) says the work includes a counterexample to a 1992 conjecture of Graham. The paper text I read does not mention pebbling or Cartesian products; the Graham-related section concerns spanning subgraphs of the d-cube of diameter d (Erdős–Hamburger–Pippert–Weakley, Graham–Harary, Bouabdallah–Delorme–Djelloul). Recorded because the name matches and the work is AI-based. It is a different problem.
events.delivers: Not this problem. On the excerpts I saw, it concerns hypercube diameter and spanning subgraphs.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.doubts: Whether the 1992 'Graham conjecture' in the CERMICS summary is the hypercube problem or another Graham conjecture is unverified. Either way it is not the pebbling conjecture.
events.direction: Not applicable to this problem.

events.what_happened: Pulaj, Wood and Yerger, 'Bilevel Programming for Pebbling Numbers of Lemke Graph Products' (arXiv 2411.19314, v1 28 Nov 2024, the only version; 14 pp; Davidson College). Theorem 1: for all 22 (up to isomorphism) 8-vertex Lemke graphs L′, L″, the support-restricted pebbling number π₄(L′□L″) ≤ π(L′)π(L″) = 64, where π₄ counts only configurations on at most four vertices. The authors present this as strong evidence of consistency with Graham's conjecture, not as a proof. Computations use a bilevel MILP on CPLEX 12.10; the paper says results 'could be prone to floating point arithmetic error', that about 37 instances hit a 30-minute cap and were rerun with a changed leader objective, and proposes future exact verification (SCIP with VIPR certificates, cvc5, QCSP solvers), which it does not report as done.
events.delivers: For the 22 pairs of 8-vertex Lemke graphs, π₄(L′□L″) ≤ 64. Because π₄ ≤ π (a bound on configurations of support at most four is weaker than the full bound), this does not bound the full π(L′□L″) and so does not test the product inequality for those pairs. It is a check on one restricted quantity for one finite family.
events.remains: The unrestricted π(L′□L″) for those pairs (including L□L and the 64 threshold), every other pair of graphs, and the general inequality.
events.doubts: The bound is computed with CPLEX in floating-point arithmetic and has no exact verification. It bounds only the support-restricted quantity. Thirty-seven instances needed a rerun after hitting a time cap. Not peer reviewed (no journal reference).
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture (π₄ ≤ 64 for those pairs). It does not test the unrestricted quantity that the conjecture uses.

ai.disclosed_cost: CPLEX 12.10 bilevel MILP; about 37 instances hit a 30-minute cap (per the paper). Code and timing data in a public GitHub repository (per the paper). Compute, not AI.

disputes.summary: The 85 bound on π(L□L) is attributed to 'Cusack and Bekmetjev (arXiv 1905.08683)' in one search summary and to 'Kenter, Skipper, Wilson' in another. The arXiv listing gives Kenter, Skipper and Wilson. Cusack and Bekmetjev are authors of the 2016 Hope College poster, not of that arXiv paper.

The history of the π(L□L) bound is disputed in the sources read. Kenter, Skipper and Wilson (2019) report 85, improving 91 (Kenter and Skipper, earlier model) and 108 (attributed to Hurlbert 2011). Flocco, Pulaj and Yerger (2023) state in their introduction that they 'prove π(L□L) ≤ 96, improving the upper bound of 108', and in the part I read do not mention the 85 bound. The 108 figure is not visible in Hurlbert's abstract. Which bound is the best known is therefore unclear from the record.

Gao and Yin are said in search summaries to have proved the conjecture for L□K_n, and separately to have proved a tree-factor case. I could not retrieve any Gao–Yin paper. The 2016 Hope poster only states an aim to prove the L_k□K_n case. No verified source records a proof for L□K_n.

Xia, Pan, Xu and Cheng (2017) is listed as Ars Combinatoria 132 (2017) by DBLP, under a slightly different title (from a search excerpt). A search summary said Journal of Combinatorial Optimization. I found no support for JCO.

The Palestine Journal 2025 abstract (Sreedevi, Kalra, Parthiban), as excerpted by a search tool, claims a 2t-pebbling property for all bipartite graphs. This conflicts with the literature the search returned, which lists the all-bipartite 2-pebbling question as open. The full text could not be read to resolve the conflict.

summary: The problem is Graham's conjecture that the standard pebbling number of a Cartesian product of connected graphs is at most the product of the factors' pebbling numbers. I ran 50 web searches (listed verbatim below), opened 27 primary or near-primary sources (arXiv abstracts and some full HTML bodies, the Wikipedia page, repository and journal pages), and read a further set of search excerpts where the publisher page was not reachable (DOAJ and De Gruyter returned 403 and 405; the PJM 2025 PDF and the Cusack et al. 2019 PDF are compressed binaries). The record finds no settlement, no bound on the conjecture's own quantity over all graphs, and no new family of cases since 26 January 2024 that I could verify. The in-window events are: (a) Pulaj, Wood and Yerger (arXiv 2411.19314, Nov 2024), which proves π₄ ≤ 64 for all 22 pairs of 8-vertex Lemke graphs, where π₄ restricts to configurations on at most four vertices; because π₄ ≤ π this does not bound the full number and is explicitly not a proof; (b) a 2025 PJM abstract on 2t-pebbling of bipartite graphs framed by the conjecture, which I could not read in full and whose all-bipartite claim conflicts with the literature I saw; and (c) neighbouring pebbling papers (snark bounds, weight-function methods, a Herscovici-conjecture paper, and a 2026 seminar titled after the conjecture that claims nothing new about it). Earlier in the record, the main positive results for the standard conjecture are special families: the odd-cycle and middle-graph cases (Xia et al. 2014 and 2017, with an odd two-pebbling hypothesis in the 2014 case), complete-graph and complete-bipartite H of large order (Pleanmani 2019 and 2020), the Lemke-square computations (Kenter et al. 2019 with 85; Flocco et al. 2023 with 96), and general bounds weaker than the conjecture (Asplund, Hurlbert and Kenter 2018, factor 2; Pleanmani, Nupo and Worawiset 2022, factor 2 − 1/min). Two variant-level falsity claims exist (Herscovici, Hester and Hurlbert 2009, alternate pebbling number; threshold and rubbling versions in search excerpts), and none of them is the standard quantity. The close calls are: whether the Pulaj et al. support-restricted result counts as a case of the conjecture (I read it as a restricted instance, not a case, since π₄ ≤ π gives no bound on π); whether the Pleanmani 2019 and 2020 results count as cases (they cover H in a class of large order, which I read as a family rather than a single instance); and whether the Li and Ye 2020 square-of-path result counts (its exact statement is unverified because I read only a search excerpt). AI involvement: no source I read credits any AI system with work on this conjecture. The AI searches (queries 6, 12, 13, 14, 20, 39, 40, 43 and others) found AI results on Erdős problems, FrontierMath Open Problems, a Google Gemini Deep Think case-study paper that lists no pebbling entry, and a 2026 news item about GPT-5.6 that concerns a different conjecture (Dinitz–Garg–Goemans) and is unverified. The PatternBoost paper (Charton, Ellenberg, Wagner, Williamson, Nov 2024) uses transformers with local search and is recorded as a different problem: its Graham-related counterexample concerns hypercube diameter, not pebbling. The Pulaj et al. 2024 and Flocco et al. 2023 papers, the two in-window and near-window computational papers closest to the conjecture, use CPLEX and Gurobi, and neither credits AI. Wikipedia's Graph pebbling article (last edited 25 Dec 2025) lists Chung (1989) and Pleanmani (2019) and still calls the conjecture unsolved. Chung's 1989 original was not reachable, so the origin of the conjecture rests on secondary attributions. The Milans and Clark complexity result (π(G) ≤ k is Π₂ᵖ-complete) is background and was not opened.
competing_reading: Pulaj, Wood and Yerger (2024) could be read as a substantive, computer-assisted case of the conjecture: it covers all 22 pairs of the 8-vertex Lemke graphs, which are the most likely counterexample candidates, and it reports consistency with 64 for each pair. On that reading it is a finite-family case with real content. The reading I think is more defensible is that it bounds a quantity (configurations on at most four vertices) that is at most π, so it leaves the full product inequality for those pairs untested, and its CPLEX computation is floating-point and not exactly verified. Separately, the Pleanmani 2019 and 2020 results could be read as settling an infinite family of pairs (any G with H complete of large order) and so as real progress on the universal claim for that family, rather than as single cases. The 2025 PJM abstract, if its all-bipartite claim is correct, would be a strong structural result, but I could not read its theorems.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of Sreedevi, Kalra and Parthiban (PJM 14, 2025): the actual theorems and whether any product inequality is proved, and whether the all-bipartite claim is correct. (2) Pulaj, Wood and Yerger's exact verification, if it appears (SCIP/VIPR or cvc5 certificates), and whether any later paper bounds the unrestricted π(L□L) at 64 or above. (3) Gao and Yin's paper, to settle the L□K_n and tree-factor attributions. (4) The Li and Ye (2020) full statement, to fix the pairing for P_{2n}^2. (5) The Pleanmani 2019 and 2020 thresholds for 'sufficiently large', and the Asian-European 2022 Worawiset note. (6) Any post-2024 paper that cites 1905.08683 or 2411.19314 and states an unrestricted π(L□L) value, or a counterexample pair, which would decide the Lemke-square question directly. (7) Chung's 1989 paper, for the original form of the conjecture (connectedness, and whether it was stated for all graphs).

judgement.why: The statement names one conjecture, π(G□H) ≤ π(G)π(H) for all graphs. Pre-snapshot family results (odd cycles/middle graphs, large complete and complete bipartite H, squares of even paths) are cases; the general factor-2 and (2−1/min) inequalities are bounds on the universal claim. Bounds and exact values for individual Lemke products (108, 91, 85, 96) concern finitely many pairs and are instances; the Pulaj–Wood–Yerger 2024 result is also instances, and further it bounds only the support-restricted π₄ ≤ π, so it does not even test those pairs. The close call was the PJM 2025 bipartite paper: from the excerpt it proves a 2-pebbling-type property, not a product inequality, so it is none and doubtful. PatternBoost concerns a different Graham conjecture and is a variant. No event credits any AI system.
judgement.doubts: Li–Ye 2020 is read only from an excerpt; its exact pairing of factors is unverified, though it is pre-snapshot either way. If the full PJM 2025 text proves a product inequality for a bipartite class, that would be a post-snapshot case; the record cannot say.
